meta.title: Qualtrics EX Scoping

questions.question: What are the top three business outcomes you expect from Qualtrics EX (for example lower regretted attrition, higher engagement, better onboarding, stronger managers, SuccessFactors adoption)? Please rank them.
questions.why: Outcomes decide which use cases go first and how success is judged.
questions.keyLabel: Top 3 business outcomes expected from EX

questions.question: Who is the executive sponsor, and what decision rights do they hold over scope, budget and the go-live date?
questions.why: Avoids stalled decisions in a 3-4 month window.

questions.question: Which employee listening tools, vendors and programmes run today (engagement, pulse, onboarding, exit, 360)? Please share the last 24 months of results, response rates and survey instruments.
questions.why: Gives baselines and reusable content. Qualtrics itself advises gathering previous reports as a reference point.
questions.keyLabel: Current listening tools, results and baselines

questions.question: Which existing survey programmes must be replaced, kept, or run in parallel at go-live?
questions.why: Drives migration, trend continuity and communication.

questions.question: Workforce profile: headcount, countries, legal entities, worker types (employees, contingent, interns), share of shift or deskless staff, and languages spoken.
questions.why: Sizes licences, languages, delivery channels and test scope.

questions.question: Is the go-live date fixed? What drives it (contract start, board commitment, business event) and what is the cost of moving it by four weeks?
questions.why: Tells us whether to cut scope or move the date when trade-offs appear.
questions.keyLabel: Is the go-live date fixed, and why?

questions.question: Which other programmes compete for the same HR, HRIS, IT and communications people over the next four months (other SF module go-lives, payroll cycles, M&A, restructuring)?
questions.why: Capacity clashes are a leading cause of slippage.

questions.question: Who will own EX after go-live (HR, People Analytics, IT, Internal Comms) and how large is the run team?
questions.why: The design must match the team that will operate it.

questions.question: Is there an EX framework, employee value proposition or people strategy that survey content and dashboards should align to?
questions.why: Keeps content and reporting consistent with strategy.

questions.question: What has worked or failed in past listening efforts (low participation, survey fatigue, no visible action, trust issues)?
questions.why: Prevents repeating known failures.

questions.question: Is Qualtrics already used elsewhere in the organisation (CX, brand, research)? If so, share tenant details, data centre and existing administrators.
questions.why: Lets us reuse existing tenant, SSO and security approvals.

questions.question: For each use case on the Use Case Map tab, mark Wave 1 (go-live), Phase 2, or Out of scope.
questions.why: The core scoping decision; everything else follows from it.
questions.keyLabel: Mark each use case Wave 1 / Phase 2 / Out

questions.question: For each in-scope use case, who is the business owner, who is the audience, and what decision will the data drive?
questions.why: A use case without an owner and a decision becomes shelfware.

questions.question: If only one or two use cases could be live in 3-4 months, which would they be and why?
questions.why: Forces a realistic minimum viable launch.
questions.keyLabel: Minimum viable launch if time is tight

questions.question: Which use cases depend on SuccessFactors modules that are not yet live, and could they start with a file-based or manual trigger?
questions.why: Lets lifecycle use cases launch without waiting for every module.
questions.keyLabel: Use cases blocked by modules not yet live

questions.question: Beyond the standard list, are there other use cases (M&A integration, return-to-office, restructuring, safety culture, well-being, inclusion, SuccessFactors adoption)?
questions.why: Surfaces ad hoc needs early so the design stays flexible.

questions.question: Which populations are in scope for each use case (all employees, countries, entities, job families, new joiners, leavers, contingent workers)?
questions.why: Determines the participant file, licences and legal review.

questions.question: How often must each use case run (annual, quarterly, event-triggered, always-on), and what are the blackout periods (year-end, payroll, appraisal cycles, local holidays)?
questions.why: Builds the listening calendar and avoids fatigue and clashes.

questions.question: Will one listening calendar govern engagement, pulse and lifecycle surveys, and who owns it?
questions.why: Caps total surveys per employee and avoids overlap.

questions.question: Which surveys should be tied to the SF PMGM cycle (for example 360 feedback inside the performance cycle, or a post-review pulse)?
questions.why: Aligns timing and avoids stacking requests on managers.

questions.question: How is Qualtrics EX contracted: SAP Endorsed Apps agreement, directly with Qualtrics, or via a reseller? Which products or SKUs (Engagement, Pulse, Onboarding, Exit, 360, Lifecycle, Employee Technology Experience)?
questions.why: Licensed products set what can be configured and when. SAP and Qualtrics announced an Endorsed Apps route in January 2025.

questions.question: What are the licensed participant counts per product, and the contract start date and term? Does the licence start before the build begins?
questions.why: A late licence start blocks tenant access and build.

questions.question: Is the Qualtrics tenant (brand) already provisioned, and in which data centre region?
questions.why: Region drives data residency and is hard to change later.

questions.question: Are AI features (Qualtrics Assist, text analytics, conversational feedback) licensed, and permitted under your internal AI policy?
questions.why: AI features may need separate approval.

questions.question: What budget is approved for implementation, change management, translation and run costs (admin effort, partner support)?
questions.why: Sets realistic scope.

questions.question: Who is the implementation partner, and which SAP and Qualtrics contacts (account executives, solution architects) are engaged?
questions.why: Shows who can unblock licence, tenant and integration questions.

questions.question: What is the status of procurement, vendor risk assessment and data processing agreements for Qualtrics, and how long do these normally take?
questions.why: Security and legal reviews can exceed eight weeks.
questions.keyLabel: Procurement and vendor risk review status

questions.question: Are there other costs to plan for: integration middleware (SAP BTP / Integration Suite), SSO, premium support, benchmarks?
questions.why: Avoids late surprises.

questions.question: Is there an existing engagement model or index (composite index, eNPS, drivers)? Must trend continuity with historical results be preserved?
questions.why: Changing items breaks year-on-year comparison.

questions.question: Will you use the Qualtrics best-practice engagement library, a custom model, or a hybrid? Who approves final content?
questions.why: Decides build effort, translation scope and approval path.

questions.question: Census or sample? What participation target do you set, and what was achieved last time?
questions.why: Sets licence volume, reminder strategy and success KPI.

questions.question: Which results cuts are required (org unit, location, job level, tenure, age band, gender, manager)? What is the minimum group size for reporting?
questions.why: Drives data attributes needed from EC and the anonymity threshold.
questions.keyLabel: Reporting cuts and minimum group size

questions.question: Will the survey be anonymous or confidential? Will SF attributes be attached to responses, and how will employees be told?
questions.why: The promise made to employees must match the technical design.

questions.question: Is benchmarking required (internal, industry, external)? Against which peer groups?
questions.why: Determines licensed benchmark content and comparisons.

questions.question: Who sees results (executives, HRBPs, all people managers), and when? What is the cascade process?
questions.why: Defines roles, dashboard design and release gates.

questions.question: How will open-text comments be handled: languages, redaction of names, and escalation of sensitive content (harassment, safety)?
questions.why: Duty-of-care and anonymity obligations.

questions.question: What are managers expected to do with results (action plans, deadlines, tracking)? Should plans link to SF goals or development plans?
questions.why: Closing the loop is what makes engagement credible.

questions.question: What survey window and reminder pattern are planned, and how will frontline or deskless staff take part (mobile, kiosk, QR code, personal links)?
questions.why: Participation fails when access is not designed in.

questions.question: Do you expect to link engagement to attrition, performance (PMGM ratings) or other HR outcomes, and is that permitted by policy and employee representatives?
questions.why: Joining survey and HR data is valuable but needs legal and trust safeguards.
questions.keyLabel: Linking engagement to attrition or performance

questions.question: Which pulse programmes do you need (always-on, quarterly, topic-based, post-event, manager pulse)?
questions.why: Defines templates, licences and cadence.

questions.question: Who may launch a pulse (central HR only, or delegated to HRBPs and managers)? What caps prevent fatigue (maximum surveys per employee per quarter)?
questions.why: Governance prevents survey overload.
questions.keyLabel: Who can launch a pulse, and fatigue limits

questions.question: How will respondents be sampled (full population, random sample, rotating cohorts)?
questions.why: Affects participant lists and statistical validity.

questions.question: Who curates the standard pulse question bank, and what is the target length (items and minutes)?
questions.why: Keeps pulses short and comparable.

questions.question: Which delivery channels are needed: email, SF home page or Engagement card, MS Teams, Slack, SMS, mobile, QR codes?
questions.why: Channels determine integration effort and response rates.

questions.question: For ad hoc, event-driven pulses (restructuring, policy change, SuccessFactors go-live), what approval workflow and turnaround time are expected?
questions.why: Speed versus control trade-off.

questions.question: Should low scores trigger real-time alerts or cases to HRBPs or managers? Which case or ticketing system would receive them?
questions.why: Defines workflow and integration scope.

questions.question: Who sees pulse results, at what minimum group size, and how quickly after close?
questions.why: Sets expectations and dashboard design.

questions.question: Which lifecycle moments are in scope: candidate, pre-boarding, Day 1 / 30 / 90 / 180, probation end, promotion, transfer, return from leave, manager change, exit (voluntary or involuntary), alumni?
questions.why: Each moment needs a trigger, template and owner.
questions.keyLabel: Which lifecycle moments are in scope

questions.question: For each moment, what is the EC trigger (hire date, position start, event reason, employment status, termination date)? Which event reasons apply?
questions.why: Triggers must be reliable and mapped to configured event reasons.
questions.keyLabel: EC trigger and event reasons per moment

questions.question: Is SAP SuccessFactors Onboarding (or another tool) live at go-live? If not, what is the system of record for new-hire tasks and data?
questions.why: Determines whether onboarding surveys can use task or milestone data.

questions.question: What are the monthly hiring volumes by country, and what survey cadence is wanted (days since hire) for new hire, manager and buddy?
questions.why: Sizes the programme and tells us if results will reach reportable group sizes.

questions.question: How should exit surveys work: which exit types are included (resignation, retirement, dismissal, contract end), and should they be sent before or after the last day?
questions.why: Exit timing and exclusions are sensitive and legal-critical.

questions.question: After offboarding, how will leavers be reached (personal email) and what are the policy and legal limits on holding that data and on alumni contact?
questions.why: Corporate email is often disabled at exit.

questions.question: Will a self-service survey complement or replace HR-led exit interviews? Is manager input about the leaver required?
questions.why: Defines the exit experience and data model.

questions.question: Is Recruiting Management in scope and live? At which stages should candidate surveys trigger (applied, interviewed, offered, declined, hired), and what applicant-privacy limits apply?
questions.why: Candidate data often sits in a different system with different privacy rules.

questions.question: Are surveys needed for internal moves, promotions, return from leave or manager change?
questions.why: Candidate Phase 2 moments.

questions.question: When a new hire or leaver raises a serious issue (harassment, safety, discrimination), who is notified, how fast, and what happens to anonymity?
questions.why: Duty-of-care protocol must exist before launch.

questions.question: Do managers see onboarding and exit results for their teams, and under what anonymity rules?
questions.why: Balances insight and confidentiality.

questions.question: How reliable are hire and termination dates, business email and manager assignment in EC today? Are back-dated, future-dated or mass-uploaded records common?
questions.why: Lifecycle triggers fire on this data; poor quality means missed or wrong surveys.

questions.question: What annual volumes do you expect for each lifecycle type?
questions.why: Sizes testing and licences.

questions.question: Which countries have specific rules for onboarding or exit surveys (consultation, consent, restricted data)?
questions.why: Avoids country-level blocks on go-live.

questions.question: Is 360 in scope for go-live? What is its purpose: development only, leadership assessment, talent-review input, or performance input?
questions.why: Purpose sets confidentiality, report design and legal review.

questions.question: SF PMGM is already live. Does it already run multi-rater or 360 feedback? Which tool will be the system of record for 360 (Qualtrics 360 or PMGM), and what drives the choice?
questions.why: Avoids two competing 360 processes and duplicated rater fatigue.

questions.question: Who are the subjects (all managers, senior leaders, high potentials)? How many, and how often (annual, cycle-aligned)?
questions.why: Sizes licences and workload.

questions.question: Which workflow model applies: predefined subject-evaluator pairs, subject nominates from a predefined list, or open nomination? Is manager approval of raters required?
questions.why: These are the standard Qualtrics 360 workflows and each needs different data.
questions.keyLabel: Rater workflow: predefined, nominated or open

questions.question: Which rater categories (manager, peers, direct reports, skip-level, customers, external) and what minimum raters per category before results show?
questions.why: Anonymity depends on minimums.

questions.question: Should the project run in waves (nominations, evaluations, report release), and how long should each wave last?
questions.why: Qualtrics recommends waves for 360 projects; durations drive the calendar.

questions.question: Is there a leadership competency model? How many competencies and items, which rating scale, which open-ended questions, which scoring categories, and which translations?
questions.why: Question set and scoring categories must be final before build.
questions.keyLabel: Competency model, rating scale and languages

questions.question: How will subject and evaluator data be derived from EC: reporting lines, dotted-line or matrix managers, project teams?
questions.why: Rater lists are the main data dependency of 360.

questions.question: What should subject reports contain, and who sees them (subject, manager, HRBP, coach)? Are norm groups or benchmarks needed?
questions.why: Drives report design and access rules.

questions.question: How do 360 results flow to development plans (SF Succession & Development, Learning) or stay outside SF?
questions.why: Defines integration and confidentiality.

questions.question: Who writes invitation and reminder messages, in which languages, and who coaches subjects on results?
questions.why: Messaging and coaching drive trust and quality.

questions.question: Are external evaluators (customers, vendors) or contingent workers included, and how is their data handled?
questions.why: External participants have different data and access needs.

questions.question: May 360 results be used in talent, promotion or pay decisions? What do the legal team and employee representatives say?
questions.why: Use of results changes legal and consultation requirements.

questions.question: Which subjects will pilot, and when? What success criteria would let you scale?
questions.why: A small pilot lowers launch risk.

questions.question: Is manager effectiveness a named use case (upward feedback, manager pulse, manager scorecard)?
questions.why: Decides content and reporting scope.

questions.question: What must managers do after results arrive: required action plans, deadlines, tracking and nudges?
questions.why: Defines the action-planning module scope.

questions.question: Do you have manager development content (internal or from Qualtrics) to recommend alongside results? Should it link to SF Learning?
questions.why: Turns insight into help.

questions.question: How is a manager defined for reporting (direct reports, full hierarchy roll-up, matrix)? What happens when a manager has fewer reports than the minimum group size?
questions.why: Small teams are the most common anonymity problem.
questions.keyLabel: How a manager is defined; small teams

questions.question: What follow-up applies to low-scoring teams (HRBP involvement, targeted support)?
questions.why: Defines escalation rules.

questions.question: Who tracks action-plan completion, and how is it reported to executives?
questions.why: Accountability for outcomes.

questions.question: Should action plans link to SF goals, PMGM or development plans?
questions.why: Decides the return integration to SF.

questions.question: How many managers need access, and will they use dashboards (SSO) or receive PDFs or emails?
questions.why: Drives licence, role and SSO design.

questions.question: Who will train managers to read results and run team discussions? Are conversation guides needed?
questions.why: Manager capability decides whether action happens.

questions.question: Is Employee Technology Experience in scope? Which tools and services (laptops, VPN, collaboration, service desk, SuccessFactors itself)?
questions.why: Decides if IT-side stakeholders join discovery.

questions.question: Who owns it (CIO, service desk, digital workplace) and is there sponsor and budget?
questions.why: Needs an owner outside HR.
questions.keyLabel: Owner outside HR for technology experience

questions.question: Which ITSM or ticketing tool is in use (ServiceNow, Jira, other)? Should low scores create tickets?
questions.why: Closing the loop on IT issues needs integration.

questions.question: What triggers these surveys: ticket closure, device refresh, a new SF release, or a periodic cycle?
questions.why: Defines event sources.

questions.question: Do you want to measure employee and manager experience of SuccessFactors itself (EC self-service, PMGM, new modules) right after go-live?
questions.why: Fast win that also supports adoption.

questions.question: Is device, location or application data beyond EC needed for segmentation?
questions.why: Adds data sources.

questions.question: Which technology KPIs are targeted (satisfaction, effort, time-to-resolve)?
questions.why: Aligns metrics.

questions.question: Which languages are required per use case? What is the source language, translation method (human, machine plus review) and who validates?
questions.why: Translation lead time can decide the go-live date.

questions.question: Which rating scales and wording standards must be used (5, 7 or 10 point, agree/disagree, eNPS) to stay comparable with history?
questions.why: Standardising early avoids rework.

questions.question: Which demographic attributes come from SF (hidden metadata) and which are asked? Are any categories restricted in certain countries (gender, ethnicity, age, disability)?
questions.why: Legal and privacy constraints vary by country.

questions.question: What privacy notice, consent text and mandatory statements must appear on each survey?
questions.why: Must be reviewed before build.

questions.question: What branding is required (logo, colours, tone) and which accessibility standard (for example WCAG) must surveys meet?
questions.why: Quick to define now and costly later.

questions.question: What accessibility needs exist (screen readers, low bandwidth, shift workers, kiosks)?
questions.why: Ensures every employee can respond.

questions.question: What survey length targets apply, and who signs off on content?
questions.why: Controls fatigue and approval time.

questions.question: Will you use Qualtrics best-practice libraries (engagement, onboarding, exit, 360, well-being, candidate) as the baseline, and how much customisation is allowed?
questions.why: Libraries speed delivery; customisation adds testing and translation.

questions.question: Which scoring conventions apply (favourable %, mean, top-box)?
questions.why: Keeps analytics consistent.

questions.question: Would you accept AI-assisted follow-up questions on vague comments (conversational feedback)?
questions.why: Needs policy approval.

questions.question: Describe the SuccessFactors landscape: instances (test, preview, production), data centre, EC release status, identity provider and SSO.
questions.why: Foundation for integration and authentication design.
questions.keyLabel: SF instances, data centre and identity provider

questions.question: What is the preferred method for sending EC employee data to Qualtrics: pre-packaged SF extension, SFTP file, API or Integration Center, or SAP BTP Integration Suite? Any constraints?
questions.why: Selects the integration pattern and drives effort.
questions.keyLabel: Preferred integration method for employee data

questions.question: Do you have SAP BTP / Integration Suite today? Who has the skills and capacity to build and run the integration?
questions.why: Capacity is the main schedule risk for integration.

questions.question: How often must data sync (daily full, daily delta, near real time)? Which fields need near-real-time updates (hire for onboarding, termination for exit)?
questions.why: Sync frequency decides architecture.

questions.question: How will EC events (hire, transfer, termination) trigger surveys: SF Intelligent Services events, Integration Center, or scheduled delta files? Is Intelligent Services enabled?
questions.why: Event triggers are the heart of lifecycle surveys.

questions.question: Do surveys need to appear inside SF (home page tile, Engagement card, mobile app)? On which SF home page version?
questions.why: Embedded delivery improves response and adoption.
questions.keyLabel: Embed surveys inside SF home or mobile

questions.question: Should results or action plans flow back to SF (development plans, goals, talent profile) or to a data warehouse (SAC, Datasphere, BW)?
questions.why: Return flows add scope and security review.

questions.question: Which identity standard will be used for employee access (SAML or OIDC, which IdP)? What is the fallback for employees without SSO?
questions.why: Access design affects frontline reach and security approval.

questions.question: How many Qualtrics sandbox and production environments are needed, how often is SF preview refreshed, and what is the policy on test data (anonymised or real)?
questions.why: Environments and test data decide test quality and compliance.

questions.question: What API user, OAuth, IP allow-list and permission roles will the integration need, and who approves them?
questions.why: Integration security approvals take time.

questions.question: Who monitors failed syncs, how will alerts be raised, and what SLA is expected?
questions.why: Operational readiness for run.

questions.question: What architecture-board approvals and change-freeze windows apply in the next four months?
questions.why: Freeze windows can block deployment.

questions.question: Is data needed from outside EC (Employee Central Payroll, time tracking, ITSM, other HR systems)?
questions.why: Extra sources lengthen the build.

questions.question: Do firewalls or mail filters need allow-listing for Qualtrics survey links? How is email deliverability handled (sender domain, SPF, DKIM)?
questions.why: Invitations landing in spam is a frequent launch problem.

questions.question: Do People Analytics or Workforce Analytics pipelines need to consume EX data?
questions.why: Plans downstream data flows.

questions.question: Which EC fields are needed in Qualtrics (person, employment, job, organisation: legal entity, business unit, division, department, location, cost centre, job family, level, manager, position)? Please complete the Data Inventory tab.
questions.why: The field list is the backbone of hierarchy, triggers and segmentation.

questions.question: How complete and trusted is EC data (manager, email, location, job level)? Which known gaps exist?
questions.why: Data quality problems surface as wrong survey populations.
questions.keyLabel: EC data quality: manager, email, location

questions.question: Which organisational structure drives reporting (reporting line or organisation units)? How many levels and units exist?
questions.why: Determines hierarchy build and dashboard roll-ups.

questions.question: How are matrix, dotted-line, concurrent employment, global assignments and secondments handled? Which manager and organisation does each person report under?
questions.why: These cases create duplicates and wrong roll-ups.

questions.question: Which demographic attributes exist in EC and are approved for survey analysis (gender, age band, tenure, nationality, and so on)?
questions.why: Needs privacy and legal approval.

questions.question: Who is eligible to be surveyed: active, on leave, notice period, contingent, part-time, future hires? What are the exclusion rules?
questions.why: Eligibility rules define the participant file.
questions.keyLabel: Who is eligible to be surveyed

questions.question: What contact data is available: business email coverage, personal email, mobile number for deskless staff, preferred language?
questions.why: Without contact data people cannot be invited.

questions.question: Where should derived attributes (tenure band, age band, span of control) be calculated: EC, middleware or Qualtrics?
questions.why: Avoids inconsistent definitions.

questions.question: Is there historical survey data or historical organisation snapshots to load for trend reporting? Format, volume and quality?
questions.why: Historical loads need mapping effort.

questions.question: What retention periods apply per use case? How are leavers' data deletion and erasure requests handled?
questions.why: Retention rules shape configuration.

questions.question: Are reorganisations planned between now and go-live, and how will hierarchy changes during a survey window be handled (snapshot or live)?
questions.why: Mid-survey changes corrupt results.

questions.question: Which unique identifier will be the key between EC and Qualtrics (person ID, user ID), and how will pseudonymisation be handled?
questions.why: Key design is hard to change after build.

questions.question: Are there entities or populations not on EC (acquisitions, joint ventures, contractors)? Should they be included and from which source?
questions.why: Scope and data source gap.

questions.question: Which reporting audiences exist (executives, HRBPs, managers, employees, People Analytics) and what does each need to see?
questions.why: Defines roles and dashboard scope.

questions.question: Which dashboard types are must-have: executive overview, manager dashboard, heat map, driver analysis, comparison, trend?
questions.why: Controls build effort.

questions.question: How will reports be distributed: dashboard login, scheduled email, PDF, embedded in SF?
questions.why: Affects access model and SSO.

questions.question: Who needs live response-rate tracking and at what granularity (without identifying respondents)?
questions.why: Supports participation management.

questions.question: Which text analytics and AI summaries (Qualtrics Assist) are in scope, in which languages, and do Legal and employee representatives approve them?
questions.why: AI on employee comments needs explicit approval.
questions.keyLabel: AI text analytics and summary approval

questions.question: Will survey data be combined with SF data (turnover, PMGM performance rating, promotion, tenure) for analysis? What safeguards apply?
questions.why: Joined data is powerful and sensitive.
questions.keyLabel: Joining survey data with SF outcomes

questions.question: Which internal targets and external benchmarks apply?
questions.why: Defines reporting comparisons.

questions.question: Do reports need local-language labels or corporate templates?
questions.why: Template effort.

questions.question: Will raw data go to a data warehouse or People Analytics, how often, and who holds access?
questions.why: Extra export flows.

questions.question: What accessibility and mobile support is needed for dashboards?
questions.why: Usability for all managers.

questions.question: Which custom metrics (eNPS, engagement index composition, attrition-risk index) need agreed definitions and owners?
questions.why: Metric definitions must be fixed before dashboards.

questions.question: Where must employee data be stored and processed? Are there restrictions on cross-border transfer (EU, India, China, Middle East, other)?
questions.why: Residency drives data-centre choice and legal basis.

questions.question: Has a DPIA or privacy impact assessment been done or required? Who is the DPO and when must they be consulted?
questions.why: Often a critical-path item.

questions.question: Which countries require works council, union or employee representative consultation, and what are the lead times?
questions.why: Consultation can delay go-live by weeks or months.
questions.keyLabel: Works council and union consultation timelines

questions.question: What anonymity commitments apply: minimum group size, suppression of small groups, comment redaction, and who approves exceptions?
questions.why: Anonymity breaches destroy trust.

questions.question: What is the legal basis (legitimate interest or consent) and the required privacy notice wording for each country?
questions.why: Needed before the first invitation.

questions.question: Which EC attributes are classified sensitive or restricted? Are any prohibited from leaving EC?
questions.why: Sets the data mapping scope.

questions.question: What SSO, MFA, session, admin-access and IP-restriction policies apply?
questions.why: Security configuration to design up front.

questions.question: What security evidence is required from the vendor (certifications, pen-test reports, sub-processor list)? Where does the review stand?
questions.why: Vendor review can gate access to real data.

questions.question: How are data subject access requests involving survey data handled?
questions.why: Needs a process before go-live.

questions.question: What is your protocol for sensitive disclosures in comments (harassment, safety, wellbeing risk): duty of care, escalation path, limits of anonymity?
questions.why: Legal duty may override anonymity.

questions.question: What audit logging is required (who accessed which results) and how will logs be exported?
questions.why: Compliance evidence.

questions.question: Has Legal assessed AI-based analysis of employee data (sentiment, attrition prediction) under internal AI policy and applicable regulation, including EU AI Act treatment of employment-related AI?
questions.why: AI governance rules for employee data are evolving.

questions.question: Who will be Brand Administrators and who will be EX project administrators? Brand Administrators have full platform access including the directory; Employee Insights Administrators can build projects but cannot access the directory or admin page.
questions.why: Admin separation is a core design choice in Qualtrics EX.

questions.question: Define viewer roles (executives, HRBPs, managers, regional HR, employee representatives) and map each to hierarchy-based access.
questions.why: Hierarchy-based access is the basis of dashboards.

questions.question: Who can create and launch surveys, approve content and release results? What approval chain and SLA apply?
questions.why: Prevents bottlenecks and rogue surveys.
questions.keyLabel: Who creates, approves and releases surveys

questions.question: Who may see raw comments or respondent-level data? What segregation of duties applies between administrators, HRBPs and IT?
questions.why: Protects confidentiality.

questions.question: Will joiner-mover-leaver access be automated from SF roles or managed manually?
questions.why: Access hygiene at scale.

questions.question: Which governance body oversees EX (steering committee, content council, privacy officer)? How often does it meet?
questions.why: Someone must own decisions after go-live.

questions.question: What support model is expected (employee help, administrators, vendor) and in which languages and hours?
questions.why: Prepares for go-live volume.

questions.question: How will changes to surveys and participant data after launch be documented and audited?
questions.why: Change control.

questions.question: Who sends invitations (executive, HR, manager), from which sender name and email domain, over which channels?
questions.why: Sender trust drives response rates.
questions.keyLabel: Sender, domain and channels for invitations

questions.question: Is Internal Communications engaged, and which channels exist (intranet, Teams, town halls, posters for frontline staff)?
questions.why: Comms lead times are long.

questions.question: What employee-facing FAQ and privacy message will explain what happens to results?
questions.why: Trust drives honest answers.

questions.question: What reminder cadence and tone are planned, and will managers receive response-rate nudges?
questions.why: Participation levers.

questions.question: What toolkit will managers receive to explain the survey and discuss results?
questions.why: Manager confidence affects outcomes.

questions.question: How and when will you communicate what changed as a result (you said, we did), and who owns it?
questions.why: Without visible action, response rates decay.
questions.keyLabel: You said, we did: closing-the-loop plan

questions.question: What changes for HR, managers and employees, who might resist, and what training is needed?
questions.why: Shapes the change plan.

questions.question: What training is planned for administrators, HRBPs and managers (formats, lead times)?
questions.why: Training must complete before launch.

questions.question: Which other surveys, campaigns or SuccessFactors go-live communications run in the same period, and how will they be coordinated?
questions.why: Clashing campaigns reduce participation.
questions.keyLabel: Clashing campaigns and SF go-live comms

questions.question: What local-language adaptation is needed for communications by country?
questions.why: Communication scope.

questions.question: Which SuccessFactors modules go live in the next 3-4 months (for example Recruiting, Onboarding, Learning, Succession & Development, Compensation, Time, Payroll) and what are their dates? Please complete the SF Module Readiness tab.
questions.why: Module dates drive trigger availability and test windows.
questions.keyLabel: SF module go-live dates in the window

questions.question: For each module, does an EX use case need its data (onboarding task completion, course completion, requisition stages)? Is a manual or file-based interim acceptable?
questions.why: Separates hard dependencies from nice-to-haves.

questions.question: Can EX requirements be fed into the design workshops of those other modules now (fields, event reasons, status codes)?
questions.why: Cheap now, expensive later.
questions.keyLabel: EX needs fed into other module designs

questions.question: Which EC configuration changes are planned (new fields, org restructure, position management, event reasons) that would affect the EX data feed?
questions.why: Mid-build data model changes break integrations.
questions.keyLabel: Planned EC changes that affect the feed

questions.question: How will SuccessFactors half-yearly releases be handled, and what test windows apply?
questions.why: Release regression is a known risk.

questions.question: Is the same partner implementing the other modules and Qualtrics? Where does resource overlap?
questions.why: Shared people cause conflicts.

questions.question: When do other modules cut over and hold hypercare, and how does that collide with EX testing and pilot?
questions.why: Avoids testing during SF cutovers.

questions.question: Is Workforce Analytics or SAC planned and should it consume EX data?
questions.why: Plans downstream use.

questions.question: What is the PMGM cycle calendar (goals, reviews, calibration)? Which PMGM data (ratings, goals) may be used with survey data?
questions.why: Avoids collisions and clarifies permitted data use.

questions.question: Are further EC rollout waves planned (new countries or entities) that will expand the EX population?
questions.why: Scalability planning.

questions.question: What phases and milestones are expected (design, build, test, pilot, go-live, hypercare)? Review the proposed 16-week plan on the Timeline & Risks tab.
questions.why: Aligns on the critical path.

questions.question: Who is on the project team (business, HRIS, IT, security, comms) with what percentage allocation, and who is the day-to-day decision maker?
questions.why: Named capacity beats intentions.

questions.question: What testing approach applies: UAT participants, test cases, test data and sign-off criteria?
questions.why: Defines quality gates.

questions.question: Which population and use case will pilot, at what size, and what success criteria would trigger full launch?
questions.why: A pilot lowers launch risk.

questions.question: Is go-live big-bang or phased (by use case or country)? What are the rollback criteria?
questions.why: Phasing is the best lever in a short window.

questions.question: How long is hypercare, and how will knowledge transfer to the run team work?
questions.why: Support continuity.

questions.question: Which blackout dates and holidays (year-end, festivals, fiscal close) will remove key people over the next four months?
questions.why: Holiday periods can remove one to two weeks of capacity.

questions.question: Which assumptions and dependencies does the client already see (licences, access, security review)?
questions.why: Surfaces risks early.

questions.question: What are the top risks the client perceives and what mitigation is already considered?
questions.why: Seeds the risk register.

questions.question: What project governance applies (weekly cadence, steering committee, escalation path, RAID log tool)?
questions.why: Operating rhythm.

questions.question: Which deliverables are expected (design document, integration specification, test results, admin guide, training)?
questions.why: Scope of documentation.

questions.question: What are the acceptance criteria for go-live?
questions.why: Prevents scope disputes.

questions.question: Which three to five KPIs define success at 6 and 12 months (participation, eNPS, onboarding satisfaction, regretted attrition, action-plan completion)?
questions.why: Success definition guides trade-offs.

questions.question: What baselines exist today for those KPIs?
questions.why: Without baselines benefits cannot be shown.

questions.question: What business case or ROI has been promised internally, and who owns benefits tracking?
questions.why: Defines accountability.

questions.question: What will the operating model look like after go-live: run-team size, skills, annual programme calendar, centre of excellence?
questions.why: Sustainable operation.
questions.keyLabel: Run team and annual survey calendar

questions.question: How will content and adoption be reviewed quarterly, and who approves new use cases?
questions.why: Continuous improvement.

questions.question: What scale-up is expected in 12-24 months (countries, subsidiaries, populations)?
questions.why: Informs design headroom.

questions.question: What executive reporting cadence on EX outcomes is expected?
questions.why: Governance rhythm.

questions.question: What policy governs use of results in performance, promotion or pay decisions?
questions.why: Prevents misuse and mistrust.
questions.keyLabel: Policy on using results in decisions

useCases.name: Annual Engagement
useCases.covers: Census survey of engagement, drivers and manager effectiveness with hierarchy-based reporting.
useCases.sfTrigger: EC person, job and organisation data; reporting lines
useCases.fitReason: Needs EC data only; the biggest effort is content, anonymity design and reporting roles.

useCases.name: Pulse & Ad Hoc
useCases.covers: Short recurring or event-driven surveys, including a SuccessFactors adoption pulse.
useCases.sfTrigger: EC participant file; optional SF home-page embed
useCases.fitReason: Reuses the engagement foundation; quickest visible value.

useCases.name: Onboarding
useCases.covers: Surveys at set days after hire for new hire, manager and buddy.
useCases.sfTrigger: EC hire date, position start, manager, event reason
useCases.dependsOn: EC hire events; richer if SF Onboarding is live
useCases.fitReason: Trigger works from EC; check hiring volumes, event reasons and email availability before day one.

useCases.name: Exit
useCases.covers: Leaver feedback and attrition drivers, before or after the last day.
useCases.sfTrigger: EC termination event, termination date, reason, contact data
useCases.fitReason: Needs reliable termination data and a personal-contact policy; legal sensitivity is high.

useCases.name: Candidate Experience
useCases.covers: Feedback from applicants across hiring stages.
useCases.sfTrigger: Recruiting stages, requisition and applicant data
useCases.fitReason: Depends on Recruiting being live and on applicant-privacy rules; usually a Phase 2 candidate.

useCases.name: 360 / Multi-Rater
useCases.covers: Subjects receive feedback from self and evaluators; workflows can be predefined, nominated or open.
useCases.sfTrigger: EC reporting lines, subject and evaluator lists, competency model
useCases.fitReason: Needs competency content, rater workflow and a decision against PMGM multi-rater; plan waves.

useCases.name: Manager Effectiveness & Action Planning
useCases.covers: Manager dashboards, upward feedback and tracked action plans.
useCases.fitReason: Builds on engagement; the key risks are small-team anonymity and manager capability.

useCases.name: Employee Technology Experience
useCases.covers: Feedback on tools and services, including SuccessFactors itself.
useCases.fitReason: SF-adoption pulse is a quick win; ITSM integration is Phase 2.

useCases.name: Internal Moves & Return from Leave
useCases.covers: Surveys after promotion, transfer, leave return or manager change.
useCases.fitReason: Same mechanics as onboarding; usually follows once triggers are proven.

useCases.name: Well-Being & Inclusion
useCases.covers: Targeted surveys on well-being, belonging and inclusion.
useCases.fitReason: Content and legal review dominate; the platform work is light.

useCases.name: Change & Project Pulses
useCases.covers: Rapid feedback on restructuring, policy change or return-to-office.
useCases.fitReason: Easy once the foundation exists; needs governance to avoid fatigue.

sfModules.dataTrigger: Person, employment, job, organisation, manager, events
sfModules.confirmQuestion: Which EC changes are planned before go-live?

sfModules.exRelevance: 360 overlap; post-review pulse; link to ratings
sfModules.touchpoint: 360 decision, review-cycle calendar, optional rating joins
sfModules.dataTrigger: Cycle dates, form templates, multi-rater use, ratings
sfModules.confirmQuestion: Does PMGM already run multi-rater feedback, and which tool will own 360?
Is CPM in use or planned?
Go-live date; is a manual trigger acceptable at launch?

sfModules.dataTrigger: Termination event, last day, reason code

sfModules.touchpoint: Course-completion pulse; link from action plans

sfModules.confirmQuestion: Should 360 results flow here or stay confidential?
Any rule against linking pay data to survey data?

sfModules.exRelevance: Joint analysis of survey and HR data

sfModules.confirmQuestion: Which home page version and mobile app?
Are these enabled and who maintains them?

plan.activities: Kick-off, questionnaire issued and walked through, stakeholder interviews, licence and tenant confirmed, security and legal review started
Use-case scope confirmed, hierarchy and data mapping, integration design, roles and anonymity rules, survey content and translations started
Directory and integration build, project configuration, dashboards, roles, messages, translations loaded
Integration test, UAT, privacy and accessibility checks, pilot with a small population
Communications, manager toolkit, training, support model, cutover plan
Launch Wave 1 use cases; monitor syncs and participation
Daily monitoring, fixes, knowledge transfer, Wave 2 planning

risks.risk: Vendor security, privacy or DPIA review runs past the build start
risks.mitigation: Start reviews in week 1; share Qualtrics security pack early; build on test data in the meantime

risks.risk: Works council or union consultation required in one or more countries
risks.mitigation: Identify countries in week 2; launch in unaffected countries first; prepare consultation pack

risks.risk: Other SF modules go live in the same window and consume the same people
risks.mitigation: Agree a single resource plan and change calendar; avoid EX testing during cutovers

risks.risk: EC data quality (manager, email, location) creates wrong survey populations
risks.mitigation: Run a data-quality profile in weeks 2-3; fix at source; add exception reports

risks.risk: Integration capacity (BTP or API skills) is not available
risks.mitigation: Confirm the build owner in week 2; fall back to SFTP file feed for Wave 1

risks.risk: Lifecycle triggers depend on modules that are not yet live
risks.mitigation: Use EC hire and termination events; manual or file triggers for the rest; defer candidate use case

risks.risk: Translation and legal text approval delays survey content
risks.mitigation: Freeze source content by week 5; start translation by week 6; limit launch languages

risks.risk: Anonymity thresholds not met for small teams
risks.mitigation: Agree minimum group size and roll-up rules in design; test with real hierarchy

risks.risk: Holiday and year-end periods remove key people for one to two weeks
risks.mitigation: Plan around regional calendars; book UAT and pilot slots early

risks.risk: 360 overlaps with PMGM multi-rater and creates two processes
risks.mitigation: Decide the system of record in week 2; start with one population

risks.risk: Employee trust is low and participation falls short
risks.mitigation: Early comms, clear anonymity message, visible leader sponsorship, you-said-we-did plan
Allow-list sender and domain; test deliverability in UAT; use multiple channels

risks.risk: Scope grows beyond the minimum viable launch
risks.mitigation: Hold a Wave 1 / Phase 2 line; change control through the steering committee

risks.risk: AI features not approved by Legal or employee representatives
risks.mitigation: Raise in week 2; go live without AI summaries if needed

stakeholders.why: Owns scope, budget and date decisions

tagNotes: Tags mapped to null (ALL, RPT, INT) are cross-cutting: the question is always relevant.
